source: Touhou 15 Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom, th15.exe 1.00b

playfield.note: The playfield aspect ratio is exactly 384:448 (0.857). Coordinates inside the field are centred on x and measured up from the bottom for objects.

stage01.background: purple violet mossy cliff, three moons at the top left
stage01.bullets: green and yellow square seals, yellow ring bullets

render_fidelity.background: green forest canopy (st01a) plus scrolling cloud layers (st01d), with a per-stage coloured fog overlay

stage01_fog.derivation: solved so raw forest RGB(82,137,80) matches the captured RGB(137,111,134)

known_gaps: The HUD draws the reference labels but not the heart and star icons.
Bullets use the correct sheet sprite but the per-bullet animation is not played.
Background layers scroll uniformly instead of following their own ANM command lists.
Enemy motion follows the ECL velocity but not the full accel/decel easing curves.
The HUD Japanese labels still use the project font; only the digits and Latin text come from the reference ascii sheet, because the Japanese glyphs live in a separate sheet that is not yet imported.
The spell cut-in portrait uses the reference frame timings but the portrait sprite itself is drawn from the enemy archive rather than the dedicated stage portrait sheet.
Enemy death effects and bullet break effects are not drawn.
verified: Playfield rectangle, aspect ratio and px-per-unit match the capture exactly.
Stage 1 background composition and the violet fog tint match the capture.
Background layers scroll at the rates their scripts specify, and the base layer rotation is applied.
Enemy sprites animate, follow ECL movement with the reference easing curves, and are clipped to the field.
The HUD hearts, stars and numbers use the reference sprites and the reference ascii glyph map.
All seven stages run with zero unimplemented ECL instructions.
The player ship is built from the reference sht data, fires its shooter sets, draws its options and animates between idle, walk and fire poses.
Items drop from the reference drop table and fall, attract and collect.
The engine globals every stage reads resolve, so no bullet spawns outside the field.
The spell cut-in and name plate follow the frame counts and bar formula from the reference portrait script.
The player mode and roster interfaces cover solo, co-op, classic and modern.
